#1602. Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

“But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the issue yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury quickly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

None of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also showed quality and a threat. The joke is currently on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a new reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I said to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

“Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he said. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”

Hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

There have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

And as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

You might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

That had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a new left-back in due course.

So at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

Palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

That’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

This is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

That’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

There is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472

A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

An almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez launched the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

We’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

We are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a big buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

Will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Dominic King writes that there were signs of promise in the relationship between Barcola, Wirtz and Isak in Liverpool’s win over Atletico Madrid, and all three forwards start against Fulham. Timothy Castagne, Fulham’s right-back will need to have his sprinting boots on against Barcola, who is grease lightning.

Cole Palmer has 15 goal involvements in his 15 Premier League games for Chelsea against newly promoted sides.9 goals ⚽6 assists 🅰️ pic.twitter.com/PJIU0YxIhQ

I’m having real fun. I’ve got a smile on face and I’m enjoying my football. Playing with players like [Palmer and Joao Pedro] inspire you to be better and make you do better and do well for the team. We are in a good moment and we want to keep it going.

Hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

We know it is always tough against Brentford. We can expect a tight game today, definitely. We both want to win so it’ll be a nice game.

We are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a big game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a new chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

There have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez departed for pastures new in the transfer window.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this afternoon’s Premier League three o’clock kick-offs, and home bankers would appear to be the theme of the day.

Liverpool will be strongly fancied to put Fulham to the sword at Anfield, with confidence low at the London club and new manager Alvaro Arbeloa (once a player at Anfield) already under pressure amid reports of dressing room unrest. Andoni Iraola secured his first Premier League victory as Liverpool manager at Ipswich last time out, and backed up that result with a come-from-behind win against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Chelsea host Hull City, who are unbeaten after three games and have yet to concede a goal. It is a remarkable start to the season for Sergej Jakirović‘s side, who continue to defy expectations as well as the underlying data. For all their spirit and defensive organisation, keeping out Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro at Stamford Bridge promises to be a tall order, though.

Aston Villa’s rocky start to the campaign took a turn for the better with a 3-2 Champions League victory at Club Brugge, and as the weeks go by Unai Emery’s team should grow stronger as their raft of young signings bed in. Nottingham Forest could be obdurate opponents, although Villa swept them aside in the second leg of last season’s Europa League semi-final. Oliver Glasner’s Crystal Palace were a bogey team for Villa though, with the Austrian coach undefeated against Emery having notched up some resounding victories.

Glasner’s former club Palace could do with a home win against Ipswich Town, while there is cigarette paper between Bournemouth and Brentford, two of the league’s smartest operators who play at the Vitality Stadium this afternoon. Bournemouth qualified for Europe at Brentford’s expense last season, but Marco Rose is looking for his first league win despite some encouraging performances.

#1601. Report: Liverpool transfer blow could lead to surprise January deal

Liverpool's recruitment drive looks set to continue this winter.

The Reds have spent over £650 million since winning the Premier League in 2025, but the rebuild is far from complete.

Julian Ward has taken the reigns within the Anfield recruitment team and work is now being done to action some of the club's winter plans.

Andoni Iraola's side aren't the only team looking to do business in January though, and a European giant could spoil the plans of the Merseyside club.

The potential transfer blow would frustrate Liverpool but could open the door for another deal to be completed sooner than planned.

Barcelona join race for Liverpool targetThe Reds are in the market for defensive reinforcements, and VfB Stuttgart standout Finn Jeltsch has been one of the most exciting names linked with a Merseyside move. Liverpool are one of many top European clubs monitoring the 20-year-old German defender, who has played in every Bundesliga game for Stuttgart so far this season. Several top sides are already in the race for Jeltsch's signature, but La Liga leaders Barcelona have now identified the wonderkid as a target.

The Reds are in the market for defensive reinforcements, and VfB Stuttgart standout Finn Jeltsch has been one of the most exciting names linked with a Merseyside move.

Liverpool are one of many top European clubs monitoring the 20-year-old German defender, who has played in every Bundesliga game for Stuttgart so far this season.

Several top sides are already in the race for Jeltsch's signature, but La Liga leaders Barcelona have now identified the wonderkid as a target.

That's according to an update from Ekrem Konur, who claims that Barca now consider Jeltsch a potential defensive option, with Hansi Flick an admirer of the youngster's profile.

The report does state that there are some reservations regarding the German's age and readiness to be an instant starter, meaning that he may be considered a long-term option rather than an immediate priority.

Arsenal, Inter Milan and Manchester United are all named alongside Liverpool as potential rivals for Jeltsch's signature, but Barcelona winning the race could actually do the Reds a favour.

Ronald Araujo has quickly become a key figure in Iraola's backline, but the Uruguayan is only on loan from Barcelona and a permanent move to Merseyside isn't guaranteed.

The Reds have a buy option, but there is uncertainty around whether they will be willing to pay the full amount.

If Barcelona were to make a winter move for Jeltsch then the door could open for Liverpool to negotiate a cheaper option for Araujo in January.

Ward will hope that he can be the man to win the race for Jeltsch, but if Liverpool don't sign the 20-year-old then a move to Barcelona could be a boost for the Reds too.

#1600. Gallery: ‘A show of strength’, ‘Milan are in the mix’ – Today’s headlines in Italy

Serie A action returned to San Siro on Sunday night, and AC Milan treated their fans to a five-star showing against Frosinone.

It looked like a tricky game against a side who would have gone back into the European places with a draw, but Milan put on a ruthless counter-attacking performance to claim the points.

An own-goal got the scoring going, while Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netted. Owner Gerry Cardinale left the stadium feeling content, even speaking of a Scudetto challenge.

It was important to win after Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus all picked up maximum points earlier in the round, and Inter’s late implosion against Atalanta means points gained on the city rivals too. Below is how the papers look this morning.

La Gazzetta dello Sport: “Milan: a show of strength. A superb Rabiot helps secure a 5-1 win over Frosinone. Ramos gets off the mark, and the team move into fourth place. The Diavolo, the Old Lady and a high-scoring pursuit.”

Corriere dello Sport: “Milan are in the mix. They beat Frosinone 5-1, moving to within five points of Gattuso’s side. A five-goal haul and 4th place. An own goal by Calvani. Ramos scores but then has to come off. Jashari, Cisse, and Pulisic also get on the scoresheet.”

QS: “Milan hit five and take flight. Frosinone swept aside.”

#1599. Mauricio Pochettino gets straight to work: New Man United boss meets struggling stars for the first time and vows to shift losing mentality as he takes training with players back from international duty

Published: 06:33 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 04:07 EST, 20 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to reset the culture at Manchester United as he lifted the lid on being in the stands in 1999 to see the club's greatest triumph.

Pochettino was officially appointed as United's new head coach on Wednesday and took charge of training for the first time on Thursday.

The Argentine was pictured greeting his new squad, with several stars having returned from international duty, before attentions turned to preparing the Red Devils for Sunday's trip to Anfield.

Pochettino also addressed the club's internal media team for the first time, outlining how he plans to drag this underperforming squad up the table.

'The culture is the most important,' Pochettino explained.

'Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create.

Mauricio Pochettino took Man United first team training for the first time on Thursday

Matheus Cunha and Lisandro Martinez were among those to report back after international duty

Man United will hope to hit the ground running under Pochettino when they face Liverpool on Sunday

'We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us to be close to winning every single game.'

'The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure.'

Pochettino's determination to be the man to bring winning football back to Old Trafford is in large part due to one of his founding memories of the club back in 1999 when he was a player at Espanyol.

Alongside his now trusted goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, Pochettino was at the Nou Camp to see United clinch the Champions League, thus sealing a famous Treble, against Bayern Munich.

'In 1999, I was in Barcelona for that final. That was an iconic final,' he added.

'Toni Jimenez [was there] too. We were shouting for Manchester United from there. I was so excited to see Manchester United.

'This [is the] type of game that you stay sitting in your place [for] and you're so excited because you are watching the game. That was an amazing game.

'And then what happened in the end... it's like it's impossible not to empathise with that team, no?

'That was an amazing memory that made me pay more attention to United, to [Sir Alex] Ferguson and the players that were there, that are all legends.'

That level of success feels a lifetime away from the current squad, which emerges from the international break for a trip to face bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield slumped 18th in the Premier League.

Pochettino wants to focus on the potential of his Man United squad, rather than their current Premier League plight

Pochettino is determined to shift the culture at Manchester United back to winning

The Argentine head coach was in the stands in Barcelona cheering for United back in 1999

While there are those who may be daunted trying to turn around the ship which sunk so far it cost Michael Carrick his job, Pochettino wants to focus on potential, rather than the present.

'It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club,' a defiant Pochettino added.

'Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free.

'The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure [off].

'Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back.

'When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your team-mates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

'That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero.

'I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.'

Pochettino touched down in Manchester on Wednesday morning after his overnight flight

Pochettino poses at his unveiling with United director of football Jason Wilcox on Wednesday

Pochettino knows that time is not on his side ahead of an upcoming week that sees United travel to face Liverpool on Sunday, followed by a Champions League trip to face Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday. The week is rounded out by a home match a week on Saturday against Brentford.

The Argentine head coach touched down in Manchester on Wednesday morning, taking a private jet straight after the final whistle of United States versus Haiti in Cincinnati.

From there he immediately headed to their Carrington training base where he took a tour and met players and staff, including Tom Heaton, Luke Shaw, Mason Mount and Bruno Fernandes. It is understood he left a good first impression on the players.

And yet, in spite of such a packed schedule, which saw him leave Carrington very late at night on Wednesday and reappear bright and early on Thursday for training, Pochettino is raring to go and is eager for his players to head to Anfield on Sunday convinced they can win.

'I have plenty of energy. It's a privilege to be head coach of Manchester United,' he said.

'And we are not wasting time. We need to be ready to compete on Sunday.

'Now it's not time to think about rest, it's not time to think about sleep. It's about being ready and to prepare everything to be sure that we are going to compete in the best condition at Anfield.'

#1598. Arsenal can equal two all-time Champions League records in Borussia Dortmund battle

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 09:09

Arsenal will be bidding to equal two all-time Champions League records when they welcome Borussia Dortmund to the Emirates Stadium for Tuesday's league-phase encounter.

Mikel Arteta's men reunite with the German giants 12 years on from their last head-to-head in November 2014, when the Spaniard captained Arsenal to a 2-0 victory in North London.

The Gunners could end the evening top of the Champions League league phase table too, if they overcome Dortmund and Real Madrid - who are two points clear - either lose to PSV Eindhoven or draw and fall behind on goal difference; Paris Saint-Germain are not in action until Wednesday.

Arsenal have accrued 10 points from their opening four continental games this season, overcoming Lille, Slavia Prague and Napoli and only dropping points in an encapsulating 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich.

After also navigating the entire 2025-26 league phase unbeaten, Arsenal could firstly equal their own club record of 17 straight Champions League group stage/league phase games without suffering defeat.

Arteta's men have won 15 and drawn one of their 16 league-phase games since a 1-0 loss to Inter Milan in November 2024, and they have only ever gone 17 unbeaten at this stage between 2003 and 2006.

That record streak began with a 1-0 victory over Dynamo Kyiv in November 2003, and ended when Arsene Wenger's men suffered a 1-0 defeat to CSKA Moscow in 2006.

Additionally, Arsenal have won each of their last 12 Champions League group stage/league phase games at the Emirates and could equal the English football record for the longest victorious run on home soil.

The only Premier League team to win more successive UCL league phase/group stage games at home is Liverpool, who triumphed in 13 on the spin between 2020 and 2025.

Ever since their return to the Champions League in the 2023-24 season, Arsenal have been almost perfect at home in the group stage/league phase, and their 12-game winning run is a sight to behold.

Arteta's side kicked off their triumphant streak with a 4-0 rout of PSV Eindhoven in September 2023, before Sevilla and Lens were bested in the same year.

The 2024-25 group stage saw Paris Saint-Germain, Shakhtar Donetsk, Monaco and Dinamo Zagreb conquered in North London, while Olympiacos, Bayern Munich, Atletico Madrid and Kairat Almaty fell to Arsenal's Emirates might in 2025-26.

The Gunners' only home encounter in Europe so far this season ended in a 3-0 success over Lille, and they have scored a remarkable 36 goals while conceding just three during their 12-match sequence.

Thanks to Arsenal's prolonged absence from the Champions League between 2017 and 2023, it has been almost exactly 10 years since they last failed to win a group stage/league phase game at the Emirates; a 2-2 draw with Paris Saint-Germain on November 23, 2016.

#1596. GdS: ‘Turbo Milan’ – how Frosinone were dismantled by five-star counter-attacking display

AC Milan put in one of their best performances under Ruben Amorim so far to sweep aside Frosinone at San Siro.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report by writing that Lazio, Roma and Juventus also had fun this weekend, scoring a flurry of goals in their victories, but it is Milan that might just come away from the round 12 feeling best.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Within 20 minutes, the Rossoneri had already blown the game wide open, eventually putting five past their opponents. All of them were spectacular, lightning-fast, and following the same pattern: every single one a counter-attack.

It was a throwback style of football, yet infused with the visionary approach of Amorim, making it both fresh and truly beautiful to watch. There may not be official statistics on this, but conceding from five lethal transitions feels like a record as Frosinone’s strategy certainly went beyond mere self-sabotage.

Yet, on days like this, this Milan – an enigma to its opponents, with fluid movement and interchangeable positioning – are a truly daunting prospect. When Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Luka Modrić and others perform at such a high level, we see the potential of this side.

The Diavolo have secured five wins in their last six league matches, yet in Europe, they have suffered three defeats in four games. Will Thursday’s clash against Olympiacos help restore the balance?

There was nothing balanced about the game between Milan and Frosinone. It is true that Alvini’s incredibly bold (perhaps even reckless) side tried to go toe-to-toe with their opponents for an hour by attacking, playing long balls, and taking on defenders.

Yet, beyond this emphasis on a specific style of play, one could make more concrete assessments. The coach clearly understood how vital Raimondo is to a team featuring such direct and creative wingers, Ghedjemis on the right and Kvernadze (who was rather ineffective yesterday) on the left.

Raimondo was the perfect focal point for them and without him, things had already gone poorly against Cagliari. Alvini attempted to make adjustments but got it wrong: he abandoned his 4-2-3-1 formation in favour of a back three (Calvani, Monterisi, Cittadini).

All this was undermined by a senseless tendency to push too high, maintaining a defensive line 57 metres from their own goal within a 3-4-3 setup that lacked a true striker, opting instead for a ‘false’ one in Schmid. Every time they lost possession, it resulted in a counter-attack and often a goal.

It might seem odd to start with Frosinone rather than the brilliance of Milan, but there’s no denying that the visitors played their part in the spectacle. This is a match that future opponents will need to study in minute detail, because Milan on the counter are a goal-scoring machine.

Amorim, too, has a knack for springing surprises, though as always the guessing game regarding his actual tactical setup for the day begins the moment the whistle blows. For example, it was not a back four as it appeared on paper.

Instead, the system actually gradually morphed into a 3-5-2, with Rabiot operating as a highly advanced right-sided central midfielder, almost an attacking midfielder. The key lies in the connection between the Frenchman and the stratospheric Moreira, who surged down the centre often.

Keeping everything running at full throttle was the incredible playmaking of Modrić, who also serves as the team’s primary ball-winner. So much for being a ‘pensioner’.

Milan proved flawless in exploiting both structural weaknesses and individual errors. Frosinone’s DNA is defined by a headlong, aggressive approach, but the opening goal – stemming from a sequence on the right flank involving Modrić and Rabiot – ended up as an own goal by Calvani.

Just four minutes in, and the match was effectively decided. While Frosinone usually thrive on quick, darting attacks, here the roles were reversed. Another full-pitch surge, initiated by Ramos winning the ball from Calvani and carried forward by Moreira and Rabiot, left the Portuguese player unmarked to make it 2-0.

Only a reckless back pass from Musah gifted Masini a goal to pull it back to 2-1. In the second half, however, Amorim addressed the one area that looked shaky: he withdrew Bartesaghi – who had been struggling against Ghedjemis – shifting Musah to full-back and pairing Jashari with Modrić.

It paid off immediately: Jashari broke away and fired home the 3-1 following yet another rapid transition. And that wasn’t the only one: Pulisic surged clear on his own after a Frosinone corner (4-1), and Cissé, having just come on, joined the fray at full throttle to add the fifth (5-1).

There were many top performances. Rabiot is like a freight train and deserved a goal. He had to settle for three assists (bringing his total to seven). Moreira is versatile, playing as a wing-back, a central midfielder, or a winger, much like he did for Belgium when they caused Italy so much trouble.

Ramos also moved well outside of his goal. Cissé was an absolute handful: he came on and scorrd, playing as a striker after the Portuguese felt a tweak. He did so with an effortless grace that makes him impossible for his markers to handle.

The end result is that Milan are back in fourth. The competition is fierce, but the Rossoneri are right there in the mix, and eventually, some of the others will stumble. Take Inter, for example. Frosinone need to rethink their strategy while waiting for the return of Raimondo.

They’ve overachieved so far, but now they might need to be a bit more prudent. And what about Milan? If they don’t turn their trip to Athens into a Greek tragedy, perhaps their European campaign can get back on track, too.

Struggling on the pitch, Manchester United are already preparing for the January transfer window with three positions targeted and seven options identified.

The Manchester club intend to use January to strengthen their squad. According to TeamTalk, the club's decision-makers have identified three priority positions: centre-back, left-back and centre-forward. Signing a centre-back is Manchester United's main priority.

The club already have three profiles in mind: Calvin Bassey (Fulham), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton) and Nathan Collins (Brentford).

The club's executives have reportedly already made enquiries about all three players. A permanent transfer would, however, be needed to convince any of these clubs, with a loan not being considered in these cases.

#1593. Inside the crime epidemic striking fear into Premier League stars: Terrified players paying 'protection money' and buying £20,000 guard dogs, WAGs targeted in violent carjackings and the fall of the crime family who targeted Alexander Isak

Published: 12:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 04:24 EST, 20 November 2026

The man parked up in a nondescript green Ford Fiesta cut an incongruous sight in the affluent residential neighbourhood of Casal Palocco, in south-west Rome, but no one paid him much notice. He made no eye contact and at no stage stepped from the car.

It was only after the street’s famous resident, AS Roma’s Belgian midfielder Radja Nainggolan, had his home burgled and an extraordinary £400,000 worth of possessions stolen that the player’s then wife, Claudia, six months pregnant at that time in April 2016, recalled the Eastern European-looking man in the battered vehicle up their street.

He was Vlada Djuric, a 50-year-old Macedonian of Romani descent and part of the wider Nikolov family, including his wife Zora Jovanovic, their two sons and daughter, whose highly organised thefts from the homes of top footballers would continue for more than a decade, with imprisonment deemed only a minor setback.

While the Nainggolans were blithely unaware of the criminal family’s lookout man – they’d gone to visit friends nearby for a couple of hours and hadn't even bothered to activate the burglar alarm – the assailants were primed to seize the chance.

The two sons, Valentino and Giacomo, mounted the villa’s perimeter wall, opening one door with a magnetic card and jimmying another with a screwdriver, and proceeded undisturbed through the house in 27 minutes, throwing the proceeds of their burglary into a bag as they went.

There were 15 watches (Rolex, Patek Philippe and others) valued at £250,000 and 20 pieces of jewellery, including a diamond worth £25,000. Security cameras on a landing and in an internal room filmed them but such was their confidence, they only partially covered their faces.

Former Roma midfielder Radja Nainggolan and his then wife Claudia, who was six months pregnant, were the targets of a burglary in 2016 (Source: Instagram/Claudia_lai_82)

Nainggolan had an extraordinary £400,000 worth of possessions taken, including 15 watches

It was old-fashioned detective work from a local officer, Bruno Failla, which led police to a rambling home at Lurano, a small town six hours drive away in Lombardy, at which the Nikolovs would lavishly entertain other members of the Romani community.

The watches matched the descriptions of those stolen from the Nainggolans, though it was a necklace with a Roma logo, and the pair of red shoes with Nainggolan's initials, which really gave the game away.

‘I ask again for vigilance and watchfulness, please,’ Failla said at the time, because this was the fourth time that footballers' properties in Casal Palocco had been targeted in the space of five years. But the challenge of placing footballers in a state of constant vigilance became clear fully seven years on, when another Nainggolan residence, in Antwerp, Belgium, was burgled while his relatives held a party there.

‘It is one of the most complicated and consistently challenging parts of our security work,’ one former special forces soldier now providing security for footballers tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘It’s been a big sector of our work for years now, but the movements of these clients are so public and that’s irresistible to criminals. The wealth is very evident.’

One of the sons, Valentino, was jailed for two years in 2016 and other members of his family also did time, but once out, they all set their sights on the Premier League. In 2024, they arrived in the UK via a ferry to Dover from Calais, stopped off in London and made their way north, sleeping in a Ford motorhome and travelling to target homes in a Citroen C3.

A spree of attacks ensued from them on the homes of Alexander Isak, then a Newcastle player, Wolves’ Matheus Cunha (who has subsequently been burgled again while at Manchester United), Birmingham City’s Neil Etheridge and Leon Bailey, with Aston Villa at the time.

A number of Premier League clubs, including Liverpool, Everton and United, are known to have appointed their own security teams to provide an around-the-clock presence at the homes of players who are in squads playing away from home – rather than have that in the hands of a range of private operators.

Some of the top football TV analysts are known to have sought the same security cover outside their houses when away at games.

A number of Premier League clubs, including Liverpool, have appointed their own security teams to provide an around-the-clock presence at the homes of stars who are playing away

Three masked criminals managed to slip over Bruno Fernandes' security fence and into his home in Nether Alderley, Cheshire, last month and made off with jewellery

It didn’t work in the case of Manchester United’s Bruno Fernandes. Three masked criminals still managed to slip over the security fence into his home in Nether Alderley, Cheshire, last month and make off with jewellery.

It was one of the player’s neighbours who spotted them on their CCTV system and alerted police, who arrived five minutes after the burglars had left. Some in this security sector feel that it takes the private firms' former military and special services experience to cope with the criminal gangs’ level of sophistication.

Clubs using security staff in this way is a relatively recent development. In the days of security officers like United’s Ned Kelly, who wrote a book about his 14 years with the club, the job entailed ensuring the team were protected in public, or ferrying managers and new signings around.

Many clubs still leave it to players. ‘Player-liaison staff will recommend vetted security providers but it’s down to player personal choice for obvious reasons,’ says one player agent.

'That's not always been easy,' says a former Premier League player-liaison officer. 'The players have a huge entourage: so-called experts who want a seat at the table and think they know best. Of course, social media enhances the security problem.'

The house burglars’ modus operandi pales by comparison with some of violence displayed by others who prey on the footballer set. One footballer's wife in Cheshire was driving a top-of-the-range vehicle when a moped took up a position in front of her and slowed. In her rear-view mirror, she saw a second. The driver of the third then arrived at her side window, assessing what there was to steal.

On any given day, there could have been £200,000 worth of jewellery in the car, though she was wearing neither rings nor a watch on this occasion. The three drove off.

The episode had echoes of the attempted heist which saw Arsenal’s Mesut Ozil and Sead Kolasinac carjacked in broad daylight in north London, seven years ago.

Sead Kolasinac, then of Arsenal, thwarts an attempted carjacking in broad daylight in north London, seven years ago. Kolasinac was with his team-mate Mesut Ozil at the time

Attackers go for Kolasinac after his car was 'boxed in' when approaching traffic lights

Paul Hughes, managing director of Benchmark Security Group, a leading Manchester-based protection firm, employs former police and Royal security drivers to train his clients in the art of 'defensive driving'.

In a two-hour session, they learn how to avoid being 'boxed in' – as Ozil and Kolasinac were – when approaching traffic lights. Techniques include never taking up a position in the middle lane, avoiding the outside lane if there is a central barrier, and always maintaining sight of the tyres of the vehicle in front when you slow.

'If you can see the tyres, you will always have room to manoeuvre right or left of the car in front, at speed, without hitting it,' Hughes says.

His staff are often asked to escort clients in their fleet of vehicles, which includes two Land Rovers with blacked-out windows. The firm acquired a Darkfighter Dome – a night-vision camera which is mounted on to the roof of its security vehicles – allowing them to see would-be assailants in the dark. Escorted school runs are also part of the protection they offer.

A screen which dominates Benchmark's underground headquarters, at anonymous premises in Manchester, revealed the fortresses that players' houses have become, when I visited.

It showed live feeds from the gardens of mansions which are criss-crossed by infra-red beams. An alarm is triggered in the control room if anyone not approved through face-recognition software is picked up by up to 18 pan, tilt and zoom cameras at a property.

Loudspeakers, operated from the control room, warn off intruders. A team of security staff is never more than six minutes away. A patrol is on the scene of an alert, usually within 90 seconds.

A number of Manchester United players have invested in specialised security dogs from the Leicester-based firm Chaperone K9 at a cost of up to £20,000 each, though some sources suggest demand has receded as many players have young children. Security firms have their own dogs.

Benchmark are one of Britain's most trusted operators – industry-accredited, with former senior police officers on their staff. But this is also a world in which some unsavoury individuals are looking to extract gain.

Daily Mail Sport is aware that a number of current players have paid protection money to ensure they remain safe and are not venturing out socially without having done so. The ‘panic rooms’ some install in their homes, with security card access, are a place to hide valuables.

The family who preyed on footballers for a decade will be behind bars for some time. Valentino Nikolov (pictured) is serving an initial 10-year sentence, which has since been extended

Kolasinac fought off the carjackers. Everton's Duncan Ferguson put an assailant in hospital when he tried to burgle his home at Ormskirk, Lancashire, in January 2001. ‘I’m not a hard man off the pitch...unless you try to break into my house,’ he said recently.

But the assailants in the Ozil and Kolasinac attack were part of Eastern European gangs. 'The criminal demographic has changed,' one former senior detective tells me. 'We are now talking about gangs who lack the slightest compunction about taking a life.'

The Italian family who have preyed on footballers for a decade will be behind bars for some time. The Rome lookout man’s two sons were jailed for 10 years and eight years respectively at Newcastle Crown Court last year, for burglaries including the Isak attack – sentences since extended. Their mother is doing seven years.

That court case revealed how the family had moved on from the days of old cars, screwdrivers and shinning over walls in Rome – using Isak’s own vehicle as a battering ram to force entry to his Newcastle home.

'None of the property stolen from my home was ever recovered,’ Isak related. 'The attack left me with a sense of unease and a fear it could reoccur.'

Cisse got his name on the scoresheet again just minutes after coming on, netting his ninth goal of the season. Diego Moreira set him up with a nice through ball in transition, and though the offside flag went up initially, VAR overturned it to award the goal.

After the game, Cisse spoke to both Sky and DAZN to give his thoughts on what was another very positive night for him personally and for the team. His comments are via MilanNews.

“I definitely always try to contribute in all positions, and I definitely prefer to play in my own position, but I’m always available in all roles. Which position? I won’t say (laughs).”

Where can you still grow and what does Amorim ask of you?

“I have to improve in many other areas. As always, scoring is always great. I’d also like to add a few assists for some of my team-mates, but the most important thing was always to bring home three points, and today we did that.”

Is there a team-mate you have to thank in particular?

You’re Milan’s top scorer. Will we see a bicycle kick soon?

“The overhead kick used to be my specialty, but now it’s not. Let’s hope it happens. It’s always a great feeling to score, I want to add a few assists too. The important thing was the three points, and we got them.”

How far along are you in your development?

“Right now, I’m not even halfway there. Maybe even lower. There’s still a lot of work to do to get there. But I’m in the right place, and hopefully we can get there.”

Have you ever thought about what would have happened if you had gone to PSV?

“Better not to think about it. Let’s just say that I’ve always made the right decisions with my family, and thanks go to them, to the coach, to my team-mates, and I’m in the right place and on the right path.”

“Progress is the right word, because we’ve changed coaches, and it’s never easy. We’re a great team, with many champions. We still have a lot of work to do. Milan always has our backs, and that’s very important to me.”

Club Brugge vs Liverpool is one of nine fixtures scheduled for matchday five of the Champions League, with several of Europe's leading clubs, including Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain taking to the pitch on Wednesday.

The eagerly anticipated contest at the Jan Breydel Stadium is among the seven matches scheduled to kick off at 8pm UK time, while the remaining two fixtures will get underway earlier, at 5.45pm.

A victory away from home in the Champions League would provide the squad with a significant lift ahead of their Merseyside derby later this week.

#1586. Inside Newcastle United's transfer tension: Matthias Jaissle wants greater control as he eyes a new No 10 and No 9 in January - but the next four fixtures could make or break him and the club's season, writes CRAIG HOPE

Published: 12:49 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 20 November 2026

This time, Matthias Jaissle wants his fingerprints on the bank notes. But what the head coach wishes for in January, and what Newcastle United are willing and able to give, is likely to be very different. When that happens, it rarely ends well - on the pitch or off it.

The need for reinforcement is clear, even on the back of £270million invested in the summer. Jaissle knows as much and is not afraid to say so. The rookie German has to protect himself as much as he does his club.

Because, as Newcastle prepare for what threatens to be a long and testing winter, Jaissle is revisiting the brochure presented to him in the summer. And that is the 38-year-old's concern and frustration - the prospectus for the season ahead was not of his making.

He arrived three weeks before the start of the campaign and with four of eight signings already through the door. At a cost of £110m, that quartet have started just three Premier League games between them, and each of those by teenager Sean Steur. Baz Toure and Aladji Bamba are virtual spectators, while reserve keeper Ewen Jaouen is injured.

For Jaissle, you suspect, that money was not spent as he would have advised, had he been in situ. Now, in the new year, he wants greater control, as well as a No 10 and No 9. For any Newcastle follower averse to tension, you best watch this transfer window through your fingertips.

Jaissle, sporting director Ross Wilson and chief executive David Hopkinson are the protagonists who will navigate January. At least, that is, if Jaissle makes it into 2027. He deserves that time - not least because of the turbulent and transitional situation he inherited - but the next four fixtures will potentially make or break him and the season.

Head coach Matthias Jaissle is seeking greater control of Newcastle United's transfer strategy

Aladji Bamba has been a virtual spectator and joined in the summer before Jaissle's arrival

After the visit of league leaders Arsenal on Saturday, there is a trip to second-placed Brighton, followed by a seismic home double header in the space of five days against Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United and bitter rivals Sunderland.

It is why, despite rumblings behind the scenes in recent days of potential transfer discord, Jaissle was on message - the collective, club message - when I asked him about the profile of player he might want in January.

'It's not the time to talk about the transfer window,' he said. 'We have players capable to deliver higher performances on the pitch. We have big quality, not only up front, but throughout the whole squad. We believe we can do better and this is what we now want to influence.'

However, there was a softening when I sympathised with the head coach over him being judged by a window for which he did not have ownership. Did he, then, want more influence this time?

'Now, it's a different story (compared to the summer), if you're already in and also if you have clarified your clear idea, your clear needs, it's going to be easier,' he said.

'But the transfer market is still a long time ahead, at least it feels like that right now with our fixtures. Our task, especially from my stance, is to focus on the next match and the upcoming challenges.'

Jaissle knows that his case will only be strengthened by a steadying of results, even though, conversely, more defeats would heighten the need for signings. They have lost four from six in all competitions.

The problem is that the hierarchy are on the record as stating the summer business went pretty much exactly as they wished and believed they had a squad for the entire season. There are also Squad Cost Ratio limitations. It is understood there is headroom for one player, but not the two the manager would prefer and not at a fee approaching the £51m they paid for Matias Fernandez-Pardo on deadline day.

Jaissle wants a new No 9 to compete with the likes of Yoane Wisse who has one league goal

Matias Fernandez-Pardo (left) has failed to impress so far at Newcastle after his £51m arrival

The 21-year-old forward is another problem. He is still to score from seven appearances and there is a fear he is not yet strong enough for the Premier League. Interestingly, Jaissle revealed on Thursday his dismay that he was booked during the 1-1 draw at Fulham last time out for screaming at Fernandez-Pardo to stand up.

That is not to say Jaissle does not believe in the talent of those brought in. He does. But for a coach in his first season in a major European league, he needs players who can impact today, not tomorrow. He needs, and wants, more experience. One of his first recommendations in August was to sign 31-year-old midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg. Nico Gonzalez eventually arrived in that position, but the 24-year-old looks like a player who has spent two seasons in reserve at Manchester City.

So, it is easy to see why Jaissle needs and wants more in January. It is also easy to see why he might not get it. There could be trouble ahead, and that is not just the upcoming matches.
